title: The Wizard
desc: Two runaway brothers cross the country so the younger one, a gifted but withdrawn video-game prodigy, can compete in a Nintendo tournament in California. Directed by Todd Holland and starring Fred Savage, Christian Slater, and Jenny Lewis.
tidbits: The film's real claim to fame is introducing North American audiences to Super Mario Bros. 3 months before it hit store shelves, making the movie essentially a feature-length product demo.
This was Tobey Maguire's first-ever film role, though he went uncredited for it.
The giant roadside dinosaurs the kids climb on are a real tourist stop in Cabazon, California, that also showed up in Pee-wee's Big Adventure.
Beau Bridges and Christian Slater both said in interviews they had barely any interest in video games before filming, then genuinely got hooked after playing on set.
It took until 2006 for the film to finally get an official US DVD release, after years of fans requesting it.
starring: Fred Savage, Luke Edwards, Jenny Lewis, Christian Slater, Beau Bridges
producers: David Chisholm, Ken Topolsky

title: Trailer Park Boys: Season 7
desc: The mockumentary-style Canadian comedy follows Ricky, Julian, and Bubbles as their small-time schemes at a Nova Scotia trailer park keep landing them back behind bars. Season 7 (2007) was the finale of the original Showcase run, which began in 2001.
tidbits: The series started life on Showcase in 2001 and used a mockumentary format years before The Office popularized the style in North America.
Bubbles' iconic thick glasses weren't a costume department choice — actor Mike Smith's girlfriend picked them up at a Texas estate sale as a joke, and the bit stuck.
Ricky traditionally wears the same shirt for an entire season, a quiet continuity gag the show kept up for years.
Across the original seven seasons, the cast reportedly said a certain four-letter word over 1,280 times combined — averaging roughly 46 times per episode.

The show's production moved trailer parks almost every season, filming in a different real Nova Scotia location for seasons one through four before settling into a park the crew purchased outright from season five on.
starring: Mike Smith, John Paul Tremblay, Robb Wells, John Dunsworth, Patrick Roach
producers: Mike Volpe

title: The Beach
desc: A restless American backpacker in Bangkok follows a mysterious map to a hidden island community in Thailand, where paradise slowly reveals its darker side. Directed by Danny Boyle and starring Leonardo DiCaprio in his first major role after Titanic.
tidbits: Ewan McGregor, who'd worked with director Danny Boyle on Trainspotting, was originally attached to star before the studio pushed for DiCaprio instead — a falling-out that strained the director-actor relationship going in.
DiCaprio reportedly earned around $20 million for the role, a payday tied directly to Titanic's massive success just two years earlier.
The production altered the real Maya Bay beach in Thailand to look more idyllic for filming, which triggered an environmental lawsuit and a court-ordered restoration years later.
The film's mountain-enclosed look at the beach is a visual trick — editors digitally added a mountain in post-production, since the real cove has a gap facing open sea.
DiCaprio was nominated for a Razzie for Worst Actor for the role, a rough follow-up to his Titanic-era stardom.
starring: Leonardo DiCaprio, Virginie Ledoyen, Guillaume Canet, Robert Carlyle, Tilda Swinton
producers: Andrew Macdonald

title: The Spy Who Came in from the Cold / The French Connection (Double Feature)
desc: A double feature pairing two landmark thrillers: Martin Ritt's 1965 Cold War spy drama The Spy Who Came in from the Cold, starring Richard Burton as a burned-out British agent, and William Friedkin's 1971 crime classic The French Connection, starring Gene Hackman as a relentless NYPD narcotics detective.
tidbits: Richard Burton and director Martin Ritt reportedly clashed constantly on set of The Spy Who Came in from the Cold — tension some critics believe fed directly into Burton's brooding, career-best performance.
The French Connection's famous elevated-train car chase was shot largely without permits; director William Friedkin has said he simply paid a transit official to let the crew film on the tracks.
Gene Hackman did the majority of his own driving during that chase, reaching real speeds of 70-90 mph through Brooklyn streets with live traffic and pedestrians still around.
The French Connection was based on a real 1961 NYPD drug bust that seized 112 pounds of heroin worth roughly $32 million at the time.
The Spy Who Came in from the Cold was adapted from John le Carré's own bestselling novel, later named by Publishers Weekly as the best spy novel ever written.
starring: Richard Burton, Claire Bloom, Oskar Werner, Gene Hackman, Roy Scheider, Fernando Rey
producers: Martin Ritt, Philip D'Antoni

title: The Legend of Zorro
desc: Years after donning the mask, Alejandro de la Vega must balance his secret identity as Zorro with his crumbling marriage while a conspiracy threatens California's path to statehood. Antonio Banderas and Catherine Zeta-Jones return in this sequel to The Mask of Zorro.
tidbits: Antonio Banderas trained with Spain's Olympic fencing team and practiced with real steel swords before switching to lighter aluminum ones for filming.
Young co-star Adrian Alonso didn't speak English during filming and learned all of his lines phonetically — the same technique Banderas himself used decades earlier for The Mambo Kings.
The train seen in the climax couldn't actually move under its own power; the illusion was created using an out-of-shot diesel locomotive, a bluescreen setup, and even a scale model.
A planned third Zorro film with Banderas and Zeta-Jones never happened after this sequel underperformed at the box office relative to its budget.
Zorro is widely cited as a direct influence on the creation of Batman, making this franchise something of a spiritual ancestor to the modern superhero genre.
starring: Antonio Banderas, Catherine Zeta-Jones, Rufus Sewell, Adrian Alonso
producers: Laurie MacDonald, Walter F. Parkes, Lloyd Phillips

title: Ratatouille
desc: A rat named Remy dreams of becoming a great French chef, and secretly guides a hapless kitchen worker at a renowned Paris restaurant to cook meals worthy of five-star reviews. Directed by Brad Bird for Pixar, the film won the Academy Award for Best Animated Feature.
tidbits: Pixar kept live pet rats in the studio hallways for over a year so animators could study exactly how their fur, ears, and paws moved.
The film went through a rare mid-production directorial change — Brad Bird stepped in and reworked the story after original director Jan Pinkava departed.
Acclaimed chef Thomas Keller of The French Laundry consulted on the film and personally developed the real-world version of the dish used as reference for the climactic tasting scene.
To save animation time, the Pixar team gave none of the film's human characters any toes.
No major food brand wanted to license a tie-in with a movie starring a rat, leaving Ratatouille with unusually little fast-food or snack cross-promotion at release.
starring: Patton Oswalt, Brad Garrett, Lou Romano, Janeane Garofalo, Ian Holm, Peter O'Toole
producers: Brad Lewis

title: Tomcats
desc: Two lifelong friends are the last holdouts in a decade-old bachelor betting pool, and their friendship — along with a six-figure payout — is on the line when one tries to get the other married off first. Directed by Gregory Poirier and starring Jerry O'Connell and Shannon Elizabeth, with Dakota Fanning making her film debut in a small role.
tidbits: This was Dakota Fanning's motion-picture debut, years before she became a fixture of prestige dramas.
Tomcats was the first film released under the newly formed Revolution Studios banner.
Comedian and political commentator Bill Maher has a supporting role in the film as a Las Vegas casino character.
Despite a harsh critical reception, the film more than doubled its budget at the box office, earning roughly $23 million on an $11 million budget.

A blink-and-you'll-miss-it sound gag is hidden in the film — during a collision at a charity fundraiser, the reaction sound is the famous "Wilhelm scream," a stock effect that's been quietly hidden in movies since the 1950s.
starring: Jerry O'Connell, Shannon Elizabeth, Jake Busey, Dakota Fanning
producers: Tony Ludwig, Alan Riche

title: Sixteen Candles
desc: A teenage girl's sixteenth birthday gets completely overshadowed by her older sister's wedding, leaving her invisible to her family right as she's nursing a crush on the most popular boy in school. Written and directed by John Hughes in his directorial debut, starring Molly Ringwald, Anthony Michael Hall, and Michael Schoeffling.
tidbits: This was John Hughes' directorial debut — he wrote the script after seeing Molly Ringwald's headshot and deciding she was exactly right for the lead.
Viggo Mortensen nearly landed the role of heartthrob Jake Ryan before it went to Michael Schoeffling, who later left acting to become a carpenter.
The gym used for the dance scene (and the set built inside it for Sam's bedroom) had no air conditioning, so filming happened in over 100-degree heat.
Jake Ryan's Porsche plate and Sam's grandparents' license plate are both quiet John Hughes in-jokes tied to his birthday and an earlier National Lampoon story he'd written.
Decades later, Molly Ringwald has spoken publicly about how some of the film hasn't aged well, calling certain scenes "problematic" in the wake of #MeToo.
starring: Molly Ringwald, Anthony Michael Hall, Michael Schoeffling, Paul Dooley
producers: Hilton A. Green

title: Spy Kids 4: All the Time in the World (3D)
desc: A retired spy secretly returns to the field to stop a supervillain from stealing time itself, all while adjusting to a new marriage and two reluctant stepkids who don't know her secret. Directed by Robert Rodriguez and starring Jessica Alba, Joel McHale, and Ricky Gervais, with Alexa Vega and Daryl Sabara reprising their roles from the earlier films.
tidbits: The idea reportedly came from a real moment on the set of Machete — Jessica Alba's baby had a diaper blowout mid-scene, inspiring director Robert Rodriguez to imagine a spy who's secretly a new mom.
It's the first Spy Kids film without original stars Antonio Banderas and Carla Gugino, centering instead on a new stepfamily of spies.
The movie used "Aroma-Scope," a scratch-and-sniff card gimmick letting audiences smell cued moments on screen — last used widely in theaters for Rugrats Go Wild back in 2003.
At $27 million, it was the least expensive film in the Spy Kids franchise to make.
Robert Rodriguez wore several hats on this one, serving as director, writer, co-cinematographer, and co-composer.
starring: Jessica Alba, Joel McHale, Ricky Gervais, Alexa Vega, Daryl Sabara, Rowan Blanchard
producers: Robert Rodriguez, Elizabeth Avellán

title: Dune
desc: Denis Villeneuve's epic adaptation of Frank Herbert's classic novel follows young Paul Atreides as his noble family takes control of the dangerous desert planet Arrakis, the only source of the galaxy's most valuable substance. Starring Timothée Chalamet, Rebecca Ferguson, Zendaya, Oscar Isaac, and Jason Momoa.
tidbits: Villeneuve had dreamed of adapting Dune since first reading the novel at age 12, and waited until directing Arrival and Blade Runner 2049 before taking it on.
Composer Hans Zimmer turned down scoring Christopher Nolan's Tenet so he could work on Dune instead, a novel he'd loved for years.
The desert scenes on Arrakis were filmed in Jordan and Abu Dhabi, while the ocean world of Caladan was shot along the coast of Norway.
Linguist David J. Peterson, known for creating Dothraki for Game of Thrones, developed the Fremen language used in the film.
Villeneuve reportedly got emotional early in the shoot watching Timothée Chalamet perform, realizing his casting instincts for Paul Atreides had been right.
starring: Timothée Chalamet, Rebecca Ferguson, Oscar Isaac, Josh Brolin, Stellan Skarsgård, Dave Bautista, Zendaya, Jason Momoa, Javier Bardem
producers: Mary Parent, Denis Villeneuve, Cale Boyter, Joe Caracciolo Jr.

title: Dune: Part Two
desc: The second half of Denis Villeneuve's Dune saga follows Paul Atreides as he unites with the Fremen of Arrakis and confronts the forces that destroyed his family. Timothée Chalamet, Zendaya, Rebecca Ferguson, and Austin Butler lead a cast that also includes Florence Pugh, Dave Bautista, and Christopher Walken.
tidbits: The massive sandworm-riding sequence took 44 days to shoot on a set measuring roughly 90 by 24 feet.
Cinematographer Greig Fraser shot the Harkonnen homeworld scenes using infrared cameras to give the Harkonnens' skin an eerie, translucent look.
Steven Spielberg told Villeneuve after seeing the film that its true subject, despite being set in a desert, was water and the longing for it.
Actor Stellan Skarsgård's body makeup took eight hours to apply and two hours to remove on every shooting day.
The film's release was pushed back from late 2023 to March 2024 because of the SAG-AFTRA and Writers Guild strikes.

title: The Revenant
desc: Alejandro G. Iñárritu's brutal survival epic follows frontiersman Hugh Glass as he fights to stay alive after being mauled by a bear and left for dead by his own hunting party. Leonardo DiCaprio won his first Academy Award for the role, alongside Tom Hardy and Domhnall Gleeson.
tidbits: With the exception of one campfire scene, the entire film was shot using only natural light.
When the snow melted too early during the Canadian shoot, the production relocated to southern Argentina to keep filming in winter conditions.
DiCaprio, a vegetarian in real life, ate raw bison liver on camera and slept inside animal carcasses during the freezing shoot.
The bear attack sequence was created entirely through CGI, with stunt performers in harnesses standing in for the animal during filming.
Director Iñárritu insisted on shooting the film in chronological order, believing it would help the cast's performances build naturally scene to scene.

title: The Way of the Gun
desc: Christopher McQuarrie's directorial debut follows two small-time criminals who kidnap the surrogate mother carrying a wealthy man's child, only to find themselves tangled in a much bigger and more dangerous scheme. Ryan Phillippe and Benicio del Toro star alongside Juliette Lewis, Taye Diggs, and James Caan.
tidbits: McQuarrie's brother, a former Navy SEAL, served as technical advisor on the gunfight scenes, which is why the characters handle their weapons with such disciplined realism.
The unconventional car-chase tactics used after the kidnapping were Benicio del Toro's own idea, inspired by criminals he'd seen on the show Cops.
This was McQuarrie's first film as director after winning an Oscar for writing The Usual Suspects.
Ryan Phillippe accidentally punched Sarah Silverman for real during the opening scene, knocking her out, and reportedly apologized to her for a week afterward.
Ryan Phillippe put on roughly 25 pounds of muscle for the role to move away from the boyish image he was known for at the time.

title: Scrubs: Season 4
desc: The fourth season of Bill Lawrence's beloved medical sitcom picks up as J.D. begins his first year as a full doctor while Turk and Carla adjust to married life. Zach Braff, Sarah Chalke, Donald Faison, and John C. McGinley lead the Sacred Heart staff through 25 episodes of comedy and heart.
tidbits: Heather Graham joined the cast for an extended run as quirky therapist Dr. Molly Clock, appearing in the season's first eight episodes.
Matthew Perry directed an episode of the season, 'My Unicorn,' in which he also guest-starred as the father of a young patient.
Colin Farrell, Clay Aiken, and Tara Reid all made guest appearances during the season.
The season received a Primetime Emmy nomination for Outstanding Comedy Series.
It opens with Turk and Carla returning from their honeymoon, only for cracks to appear when Carla tries reshaping her new husband's habits.
starring: Zach Braff, Sarah Chalke, Donald Faison, John C. McGinley, Judy Reyes, Ken Jenkins, Neil Flynn
producers: Bill Lawrence, Neil Goldman, Garrett Donovan

title: Scrubs: Season 6
desc: Season six follows the Sacred Heart staff through pregnancies, promotions, and personal crossroads, and includes the show's celebrated musical episode. Zach Braff, Sarah Chalke, Donald Faison, and John C. McGinley star, with guest turns from Elizabeth Banks and Keri Russell.
tidbits: The season features 'My Musical,' the show's one-off musical episode, with several songs co-written by Tony winners Robert Lopez and Jeff Marx of Avenue Q fame.
The episode's patient who mysteriously hears everyone speaking in song is played by Stephanie D'Abruzzo, herself an Avenue Q alum.
One of the musical numbers is a tango where Turk mistakenly insists Carla is Puerto Rican, sparking the running gag about her actual Dominican heritage.
The season moved to Thursdays at 9 p.m. as part of NBC's 'Comedy Night Done Right' programming block.
It received five Emmy nominations.
starring: Zach Braff, Sarah Chalke, Donald Faison, John C. McGinley, Judy Reyes, Ken Jenkins, Neil Flynn
producers: Bill Lawrence, Neil Goldman, Garrett Donovan

title: Scrubs: Season 7
desc: Scrubs' shortest season was cut down by the 2007-2008 Writers Guild strike, running just 11 episodes instead of the planned 18. It was also the show's final season on NBC before the series moved to ABC. Zach Braff, Sarah Chalke, and John C. McGinley star as the Sacred Heart staff navigate a season upended mid-shoot.
tidbits: Only 11 of the 18 planned episodes were completed once the writers' strike began in November 2007; a twelfth episode, 'My Commitment,' was left unfinished.
Footage shot for the abandoned 'My Commitment' was later reworked into a season 8 episode the following year.
The strike caused several episodes to air out of order, creating a continuity error where Dr. Kelso appears as Chief of Medicine despite having already retired earlier in the season.
This was the final Scrubs season shot in the older 4:3 aspect ratio before the show switched to widescreen.
It was also the last season to air on NBC; the show moved to ABC starting with season 8.
starring: Zach Braff, Sarah Chalke, Donald Faison, John C. McGinley, Judy Reyes, Ken Jenkins, Neil Flynn
producers: Bill Lawrence, Neil Goldman, Garrett Donovan

title: Scrubs: Season 9 (Med School)
desc: Nicknamed 'Med School,' the ninth and final season shifts focus to a new class of students at Winston University, with Turk and Dr. Cox now serving as instructors. Donald Faison and John C. McGinley anchor a mostly new ensemble that includes Kerry Bishé, Dave Franco, and Michael Mosley.
tidbits: The season was originally pitched as a spin-off titled 'Scrubs: Med School,' but the network folded it into the main series as season nine instead.
Only Donald Faison and John C. McGinley returned as full-time series regulars; Zach Braff and Sarah Chalke appeared in just a handful of episodes to help transition the show.
Filming moved from the show's longtime hospital location to newly built sets at Culver Studios, and the season was the first shot on digital video instead of film.
At 13 episodes, it's the shortest of Scrubs' nine seasons.
The show's creator, Bill Lawrence, was tied up running Cougar Town at the time, so Josh Bycel stepped in as showrunner for the final season.
starring: Donald Faison, John C. McGinley, Kerry Bishé, Dave Franco, Michael Mosley, Zach Braff, Sarah Chalke
producers: Bill Lawrence, Josh Bycel

title: Trailer Park Boys: The Xmas Special
desc: A holiday prequel set in 1997, years before the series began, following Julian bailing Ricky out of jail just before Christmas and roping him into a gift-stealing scheme to win back Lucy. Directed by series creator Mike Clattenburg, the hour-long special reveals the origins of several running gags from the show.
tidbits: The special reveals the origin of Bubbles' bubble machine, an unopened childhood Christmas gift from his parents that he'd kept sealed for years hoping they'd return.
It's set before Jamie went by the nickname J-Roc, before Randy and Lahey became a couple, and before the Shitmobile lost a door.
The special was filmed and released during the show's fourth season, even though its story takes place years earlier.
Jonathan Torrens plays Jamie in his pre-J-Roc persona, a rare appearance of the character before his more famous alter ego took over.
The special ends with Ricky delivering a drunken sermon from a church pulpit about the true meaning of Christmas.
starring: Mike Smith, John Paul Tremblay, Robb Wells, John Dunsworth, Patrick Roach, Lucy DeCoutere
producers: Mike Clattenburg, Barrie Dunn

title: The Nanny: Season 2
desc: Season two of the CBS sitcom follows Queens-born nanny Fran Fine as she continues navigating life in wealthy Broadway producer Maxwell Sheffield's Manhattan mansion. Fran Drescher stars alongside Charles Shaughnessy, Lauren Lane, and Daniel Davis across 26 episodes.
tidbits: Fran Drescher created the series with her then-husband Peter Marc Jacobson, basing much of Fran Fine's backstory directly on her own life.
Fran Fine and Fran Drescher share nearly identical biographical details, right down to parents named Morty and Sylvia and a sister named Nadine.
Drescher pitched the show after a chance encounter with a CBS executive on a flight to Paris, and the pilot was filmed less than a year later.
The season includes 'The Wine Cellar,' where Fran and rival C.C. Babcock get accidentally locked together during a birthday party.
The show won an Emmy for Fran's extravagant costume design, a signature element of the series.
starring: Fran Drescher, Charles Shaughnessy, Lauren Lane, Daniel Davis, Nicholle Tom, Benjamin Salisbury, Madeline Zima
producers: Fran Drescher, Peter Marc Jacobson, Prudence Fraser, Robert Sternin

title: MacGyver: Season 7
desc: The seventh and final season of the classic action series sees Angus MacGyver relying on his trademark improvised problem-solving through 14 episodes. Richard Dean Anderson stars alongside Dana Elcar as MacGyver's longtime friend Pete Thornton.
tidbits: The season was abbreviated: after its twelfth episode aired in December 1991, the show vanished from ABC's schedule and didn't return until April 1992, by which point it had already been cancelled.
This was one of only three seasons filmed in Los Angeles; seasons three through six were shot in Vancouver.
Richard Dean Anderson later said the show ended simply because everyone involved felt it was time to move on.
MacGyver's resourceful, gadget-free problem-solving became so iconic that his name entered the language as a verb.
Two TV movies, Lost Treasure of Atlantis and Trail to Doomsday, aired in 1994 to wrap up the character's story after the series ended.
starring: Richard Dean Anderson, Dana Elcar
producers: Henry Winkler, John Rich, Stephen Downing

title: Gary Unmarried: Season 1
desc: Jay Mohr stars as Gary Brooks, a newly divorced painting contractor navigating the dating scene while sharing custody of his two kids with his controlling ex-wife Allison, played by Paula Marshall. The CBS sitcom mixes post-divorce chaos with genuine warmth across its first season.
tidbits: The show was known internally as 'Project Gary' during its original taping before the network settled on its final title.
James Burrows, the legendary multi-camera sitcom director behind Cheers and Friends, directed the bulk of the series.
Ed Begley Jr. played Allison's new fiancé, who happens to be the couple's former marriage counselor, adding an extra layer of awkwardness to the custody arrangement.
Keegan-Michael Key had a recurring role on the show years before he and Jordan Peele launched Key & Peele.
The series was cancelled after two seasons in 2010, leaving one storyline unresolved for fans.
starring: Jay Mohr, Paula Marshall, Ryan Malgarini, Kathryn Newton, Ed Begley Jr., Al Madrigal
producers: Ed Yeager, James Burrows, Ric Swartzlander

title: Rules of Engagement: Season 3
desc: The third season follows two couples and a single womanizer as they navigate different phases of relationships. Patrick Warburton, Megyn Price, Oliver Hudson, Bianca Kajlich, and David Spade lead the cast through 13 episodes as a mid-season CBS entry.
tidbits: This season introduced Adhir Kalyan as Timmy, Russell's assistant, the only new recurring character from the season to stick around for the rest of the series.
Patrick Warburton, best known at the time as Elaine's boyfriend Puddy on Seinfeld, said he specifically wanted to break from playing purely comedic 'goofball' roles when the series began.
The show is produced by Adam Sandler's Happy Madison Productions.
In one storyline, Audrey discovers Russell secretly loves Broadway musicals and blackmails him into free theater tickets.
Despite mixed reviews throughout its run, the series survived seven seasons on CBS, largely on the strength of its later timeslot pairing with The Big Bang Theory.
starring: Patrick Warburton, Megyn Price, Oliver Hudson, Bianca Kajlich, David Spade, Adhir Kalyan
director: Mark Cendrowski, Ted Wass, Gail Mancuso
producers: Tom Hertz, Doug Robinson, Jack Giarraputo, Adam Sandler

title: The Facts of Life: Seasons 1 & 2
desc: A spin-off of Diff'rent Strokes, the series follows housemother Edna Garrett, played by Charlotte Rae, as she guides a group of girls at the Eastland boarding school through growing up. This set collects the show's first two seasons, back when the cast was still considerably larger than the four girls fans would come to know best.
tidbits: The show began as the final episode of Diff'rent Strokes' first season, an episode called 'The Girls' School,' before spinning off into its own series.
Charlotte Rae herself sang the original season 1 version of the theme song before it was replaced by Gloria Loring's more familiar rendition starting in season 2.
After the first season, the network fired six cast members and trimmed the ensemble down to the core four girls who'd define the show: Blair, Natalie, Jo, and Tootie.
Nancy McKeon's character Jo Polniaczek wasn't introduced until season 2, arriving as a tougher counterpoint to the original cast.
Charlotte Rae insisted the housemother character be named Edna, after her own warm and caring mother.
starring: Charlotte Rae, Lisa Whelchel, Kim Fields, Mindy Cohn, Nancy McKeon
producers: Jack Elinson, Jerry Mayer, Dick Clair, Jenna McMahon

title: Married... with Children: Season 2
desc: The Bundy family's second season follows Al, Peggy, Kelly, and Bud through 22 episodes of Fox's irreverent, envelope-pushing sitcom. This is the season where Kelly's trademark ditziness fully sets in and the show starts finding its comedic footing.
tidbits: The Bundy surname came from wrestling villain King Kong Bundy, who the show's creators were fans of, and who later made a guest appearance himself as one of Peggy's relatives.
The season finale, 'All in the Family,' was dedicated to Divine, the drag performer who had been cast as Uncle Otto but passed away the day before filming.

The show's theme song, Frank Sinatra's 'Love and Marriage,' was famously expensive to license, which led later DVD releases to briefly swap in a generic instrumental track before the original was restored.
This season contains the first appearance of the family dog Buck, though it's implied he'd already been with the Bundys for a few years by this point.
Al and Peggy Bundy were originally conceived with comedian Sam Kinison and actress Roseanne Barr in mind, though both turned the roles down.
starring: Ed O'Neill, Katey Sagal, Christina Applegate, David Faustino, Amanda Bearse, David Garrison
producers: Ron Leavitt, Michael G. Moye

title: The Girls Next Door: Season 2
desc: The E! reality series returns for a second season inside the Playboy Mansion, following Hugh Hefner's then-girlfriends Holly Madison, Bridget Marquardt, and Kendra Wilkinson. The season opens with a trip celebrating Hefner's 80th birthday and continues following the trio's personal and career pursuits.
tidbits: Season 2 opened with a special hour-long episode, 'Happy Birthday, Hef,' covering Hefner's 80th birthday celebrations in Los Angeles, London, and Paris.

trivia.heading: Timberlake's Tax Nightmare
trivia.text: The very first episode sent fake government agents to Justin Timberlake's house to seize his home and belongings over $900,000 in unpaid taxes. His near-tears reaction became one of the most famous moments in reality TV.

trivia.heading: Frankie Muniz Loses His Porsche
trivia.text: Malcolm in the Middle star Frankie Muniz was the show's first victim, convinced that his Porsche had been stolen from outside a store.

trivia.heading: Created by Ashton
trivia.text: Ashton Kutcher, then starring on That '70s Show, created the series with Jason Goldberg and hosted every prank. It premiered on MTV on March 17, 2003.

trivia.heading: Dax Shepard's Big Break
trivia.text: Dax Shepard was one of the original Punk'd pranksters before going on to star in Parenthood and host the Armchair Expert podcast.

trivia.heading: The Show That Wouldn't Die
trivia.text: Punk'd was revived on MTV in 2012, on BET in 2015, and on Quibi in 2020 with Chance the Rapper as host.
